statusText: Mapped policy state: BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES. Tail rises to 28% within the elevated band and Stress is high at 72%.
recommendation: Nasdaq-100 futures are at 29,142-29,148, down about 1.26% and 370 points, after printing a new session low of 29,137.50 that breaks the 29,178 base held for the previous three hours. Price is holding within roughly 10 points of that low, so the stall resolved by extension rather than by a reclaim. The cross-asset picture is aligned: the US 10-year is at 4.79%, its highest since January 2025, WTI is $87.83 and Brent $92.26 after verified projectile strikes on two very large crude carriers in the Strait of Hormuz, and VIX is 15.82, up 6% but still low in absolute terms. Tail therefore rises from 25% to 28%, reflecting a resumed one-way leg, price held near the session extreme and a genuine geopolitical discontinuity, while remaining well below the strong-block band because the move is orderly, its magnitude is moderate and implied volatility is not confirming a panic. Conditional risk stays concentrated in the narrow 13:30-15:00 UTC window covering the US cash open and the simultaneous ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS releases. The assessment would ease toward the WATCH band on a reclaim and hold of 29,330, and would move toward the strong-block band only on repeated failed retracements extending the low with widening downside range.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures break the 29,178 base to a new session low of 29,137.50, resuming the down-leg as the 10-year reaches 4.79% and Hormuz tanker strikes lift crude
body:
The three-hour stall has resolved to the downside. Two independent quote sources agree that Nasdaq-100 futures traded 29,142.50-29,148.00 at about 12:20 UTC, roughly -1.26% and 370 points below the 29,513 previous close, on a session range of 29,137.50-29,571.25. The session low was extended from 29,178.00 to 29,137.50 during this hour and price is holding within about 10 points of it. That is the material change from the previous assessment, which held Tail at 25% explicitly on the condition that no new low was made. The break is real but marginal in size, roughly 40 points, and the tape has not accelerated away from the low.

The cross-asset backdrop is coherently risk-negative and is the reason this is not being read as ordinary two-sided weakness. The US 10-year yield is 4.79%, up about 3.5 basis points and at its highest since January 2025, with the 2-year at 4.37% and the 30-year at 5.27%. This is part of a global sovereign move: Bloomberg's gauge of global government debt has reached 3.72%, the highest since mid-2008, the Japanese 10-year has touched 3% for the first time since 1996, and Australian 10-year debt is at levels last seen in 2011. The drivers reported are the Jackson Hole reaffirmation of an inflation-first stance, oil supply risk, and government spending concerns across Japan, the UK and the US.

The geopolitical leg is verified and has escalated. Two very large crude carriers, the Bahri-operated Sidr and the Sinokor-operated Senegal Prosperity, were struck by unknown projectiles in quick succession while transiting outbound near Khasab, Oman, each carrying about 2 million barrels of Saudi crude. Crew were reported safe. Reporting indicates the US president has since threatened further strikes against Iran, described as the first exchanges of fire since late July. WTI is $87.83, up 2.41%, and Brent is $92.26, up 1.96%.

Equity internals confirm rather than contradict. Delayed latest-session context shows all eight tracked megacaps lower with a mean of about -0.90%, all seven tracked semiconductors lower with a mean of about -1.53%, and technology, communication services and consumer cyclical sectors all negative. That context is delayed and is used only as confirmation, not as evidence of the live price path.

Tail is set at 28%. The increase from 25% is justified by observed evidence rather than anticipation: a base that broke to a new low after three hours, price held near the session extreme, aligned yields, oil, volatility and internals, and a genuine geopolitical discontinuity. It is held well below the strong-block band because the total decline is a moderate 1.26%, VIX at 15.82 is low in absolute terms and not confirming stress, the new low extended the range by only about 40 points, and price discovery has remained orderly throughout. Stress rises to 72%, reflecting a difficult and fast-moving but not disorderly environment. Confidence is 87%, supported by two agreeing live quote sources, primary yield and commodity data, and independently verified geopolitical reporting.

The danger window is held narrow at 13:30-15:00 UTC. It covers the US cash open into an already established down-leg and the simultaneous 14:00 UTC release of ISM Manufacturing, consensus 55.2 against 55.6 prior, and JOLTS job openings, consensus about 7.33 million. Forecast Tail peaks at 32% in that window and Stress at 76-78%, with mode projected as event/whipsaw. It stays below the strong-block threshold because event dispersion and surprise magnitude primarily raise Stress rather than the probability of the specific no-retracement path that matters here.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry a published Claude assessment. The first twenty mapped to the EA_ON band with Tail between 9 and 13 while Stress climbed steadily from 47 to 58, and dominant mode was mixed throughout that stretch: through the August 31 US session and the overnight hours, crude extended and the 10-year pushed higher after the Jackson Hole address, but the price path itself stayed two-sided so Tail remained compressed. The regime changed in the final four lookback hours on September 1. Tail moved to 22 with mode trend-down at 08:00 UTC as the overnight band gave way alongside the Hormuz tanker strikes, reached 26 at 09:00 UTC as a second leg extended with price pinned near the session low, then held at 25 through 10:00 and 11:00 UTC as that extension stalled without being reclaimed. Stress rose in parallel from 58 to 70. That stall is what the current hour has now resolved, to the downside.
outlookSummary: The base case over the next 24 hours is that today's combined rates, oil and geopolitical repricing resolves into two-sided trade rather than a persistent no-retracement path, but the projection now starts from a leg that has just resumed rather than one that is stalling. Tail is therefore lifted to 30 for the 13:00 UTC hour covering the cash open and peaks at 32 with Stress at 78 in the 14:00 UTC hour, when ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS print simultaneously 30 minutes into the session, with mode projected event/whipsaw. That peak stays below the strong-block threshold because event dispersion primarily raises Stress. The path is projected to decay from 15:00 UTC as post-release volatility ages, crossing back into the WATCH band by 17:00 UTC, with a modest flow-driven uptick in the 19:00 UTC power hour around month-start rebalancing. Tail is projected back inside the EA_ON band from 21:00 UTC, reaching a trough of 14 near 03:00-04:00 UTC before firming gently with the European handover and again into the September 2 morning ahead of ADP at 12:15 UTC. The projection would be invalidated by repeated failed retracements extending the low with widening downside range, by a disorderly reaction to the 14:00 UTC data, or by a further Hormuz escalation; it would ease early on a reclaim and hold of 29,330.
